title: Inside the controversial call that ended Game 2 of the World Series
summary: The Milwaukee Brewers lead the Tampa Bay Rays 2-0 in the Fall Classic after a checked-swing strikeout ended Game 2.
story: The Milwaukee Brewers are two wins away from the first World Series title in franchise history, and they got a little help from an incredibly close call Saturday night.

With the Brewers leading 5-4 in the top of the ninth, the Rays had a runner on third with two outs and designated hitter Yandy Díaz at the plate. On a 3-2 pitch that would have been ball four, Díaz tried to check his swing on a curveball from Aaron Ashby.

Home plate umpire Jim Wolf initially ruled that Díaz hadn’t swung, which would have sent him to first base. But Milwaukee catcher William Contreras appealed to the first base umpire, who ruled that Díaz had gone around. The strikeout ended the game.
Here’s how the swing looked in real time:
And here’s how it looked on replay:
“In the moment, yeah, I disagreed. But the umpire said it was a swing and it is what it is,” Díaz said after the game.
“I didn’t go look at it, but from my vantage point, it did look like that he swung,” Tampa Bay manager Kevin Cash said.
The postgame crew on the Fox broadcast seemed split over the swing as well.
What exactly is a checked swing?
It’s a great question, and one that MLB’s rulebook doesn’t answer.

According to MLB.com, “there is no definition for ‘check swing’ in the official baseball rules. The closest thing comes in the definition of terms where the first example of a strike is a pitch that ‘is struck at by the batter.’”
That leaves it to the umpires’ discretion when a pitch is considered to be “struck at.”

Colloquially, a batter has to break an imaginary plane for a checked swing to be considered a full one. What exactly is that plane? Again, there’s no official rule. As with obscenity in Jacobellis v. Ohio, umpires typically know it when they see it.
Why didn’t the Rays challenge the call?

Much to the delight of fans, MLB introduced the automated ball-strike (ABS) system this season, allowing players to challenge, as the name suggests, balls and strikes. ABS came on top of the expanded replay review rules instituted in 2014, which granted managers at least one challenge per game on calls such as force plays, tag plays and even fan interference.
For Subscribers
Unfortunately for Tampa Bay, checked swings aren’t on the list of reviewable plays, so the Rays couldn’t ask for a review of the play in Game 2.

“We got ABS for the first time this year, getting the balls and strikes right. We need to get a system that can get [checked swings] right,” Fox play-by-play announcer Joe Davis said during a replay of Díaz’s swing.
Will this happen again?

Given all the technology MLB has at its disposal, it’s hard to believe the league and players union will let a situation like Game 2’s happen again, particularly when the stakes are as high as the World Series.

In 2024, MLB tested checked-swing challenges in the Arizona Fall League, using the same Hawk-Eye technology used for the ABS system. In those challenges, teams were able to review if a checked swing “crossed a 45-degree threshold from home plate,” according to MLB.com.
For Subscribers
The checked-swing challenge has since made it to the minors, introduced to the single-A Florida State League in 2025 and the Triple-A Pacific Coast League this year.
In June 2025, MLB Commissioner Rob Manfred said he wanted teams to be accustomed to the ABS system before introducing the checked-swing challenge to the majors.

“We haven’t made a decision about the checked-swing thing,” Manfred said at the time. “We do try to think sequentially about what’s coming. I think we got to get over the hump in terms of either doing ABS or not doing it before you’d get into the complication of a separate kind of challenge involved in an at-bat, right? You think about them, they’re two different systems operating at the same time. We really got to think that one through.”

title: Here’s the biggest news you missed this weekend
summary: Former President Barack Obama, appearing in Ohio Saturday at his first campaign rally for the midterm elections, characterized President Donald Trump as an agent of “chaos and cruelty” and a man of broken promises.
story: Former President Barack Obama, appearing in Ohio on Saturday at his first campaign rally of this fall’s midterm elections, called President Donald Trump an agent of “chaos and cruelty” and a man of broken promises.
Obama’s visit was aimed at boosting two Democrats: Amy Acton, the party’s nominee for governor; and former Sen. Sherrod Brown, who has mounted a comeback bid for his old job.
Obama was particularly scornful of Vivek Ramaswamy’s attack ad aimed at Acton, saying there is “no line” Ramaswamy won’t cross.
Later in the night, Obama rallied for Michigan’s Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed in Detroit. The city, where 75% of the population is Black, is crucial to statewide victories.
Notable quote
He’s got the White House looking like Saddam Hussein opened a Cheesecake Factory.
Obama made pointed criticisms of his Republican successor, lambasting Trump for his focus on White House ballroom construction.
Iranian plots to kill U.S. officials have reached ‘advanced stages,’ intel memo warns

Iran has stepped up efforts to target U.S. personnel in the Middle East and elsewhere, according to a memo Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton sent to Secretary of State Marco Rubio on Friday.
The memo warned that “the lethal plotting efforts by the Iranians against U.S. citizens have reached advanced stages.”
A U.S. official confirmed the memo’s authenticity to NBC News after it was first reported by Axios.

The intelligence comes days after sources told NBC News that the U.S. military has been quietly scaling back its troop presence at bases across the Middle East. The State Department has also ordered further staff reductions at multiple diplomatic posts in the region, including in Lebanon, the United Arab Emirates, Qatar and Jordan, according to a State Department official.

Clayton told Rubio that the risk was “relevant to more individuals than are currently cleared to receive this information,” adding: “We will make every effort to downgrade as much intelligence as possible so you can share it with State Department personnel at your discretion.”
‘Meet the Press’

Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., told NBC’s “Meet the Press” that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth should testify before the Senate on the Starlink satellite limitations that disrupted Ukrainian military operations.
If Democrats retake the Senate, Schiff told moderator Kristen Welker, “Defense Secretary Hegseth should be brought in. Anyone who has knowledge of what happened.”
Michigan’s Republican Senate nominee Mike Rogers responded to Trump calling Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed a “jihadist” and a “violent terrorist.”
“I’ve never called [El-Sayed] a terrorist,” Rogers said on “Meet the Press” after being asked about Trump’s comments.
Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer pushed back on comments made by former first lady Michelle Obama last year that U.S. voters aren’t ready to elect a woman as president.

“Listen, I have got a lot of colleagues who I think are probably interested in running for president, and I’ve heard everyone say, ‘You can’t have this person or that person,’” the governor told “Meet the Press.”

title: Kimi Antonelli wins U.S. Grand Prix in Texas, putting him on the brink of F1 championship
summary: Kimi Antonelli won the U.S. Grand Prix on Sunday with a dominant lights-to-flag drive, putting him on the brink of becoming the 2026 Formula 1 world champion.
story: AUSTIN, Texas — Kimi Antonelli won the U.S. Grand Prix on Sunday with a dominant lights-to-flag drive, putting him on the brink of becoming the 2026 Formula 1 world champion.

The 20-year-old Mercedes driver fell just short of clinching the title in Texas, but he extended his already commanding lead and is on the verge of making history as F1’s youngest-ever champion in just his second season.
The Italian has an excellent opportunity to lock down the title at the Mexico City race next Sunday.
With five races to go, Antonelli sits 124 points ahead of his nearest rival with a maximum of 125 points up for grabs. The race in Austin marked his ninth victory of the season.
“It was the result we needed,” Antonelli said in a post-race interview. “We’re very close, but yeah, we trying to finish on a high and hopefully we can finish it very soon.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

Behind Antonelli, Ferrari’s Charles Leclerc finished second and Red Bull’s Max Verstappen finished third. Neither is in contention for the title. Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton finished fourth. And George Russell, also with Mercedes, finished eighth, barely staying in mathematical contention in the standings.
Even before the Austin race, Russell and Hamilton both spoke of Antonelli securing the 2026 title as a matter of when, not if.

Antonelli would break a record set by 23-year-old Sebastian Vettel, who won the trophy in a title-deciding thriller at the final race of the 2010 F1 season. Antonelli was four years old at the time and joked to NBC News that he recalls playing with Hot Wheels.
He would also become the first Italian to win the world championship since Alberto Ascari in 1953.
F1 officials counted an attendance of 467,000 this weekend.

It was a masterful drive from Antonelli, who proved once again why he’s cruising to a world championship. He started first on Sunday and sped off into the distance as Verstappen battled with the two Ferraris in the opening laps.

Antonelli pitted on Lap 25 of 56 for his one and only stop to change tires. Leclerc and Verstappen both sought two-stop strategies to try and catch him, but failed to do so. Leclerc overtook Verstappen in the final stint of the race.

And it was another weekend in which Russell, 28, was one step behind his younger teammate and rival when it counted. Russell qualified sixth and held that position in the opening stages of the race. But on Lap 9, Russell was given a 5-second time penalty for “leaving the track and gaining an advantage,” which cost him positions and eventually dropped him to eighth.

title: Woman sexually assaulted at knifepoint in Central Park, police say
summary: The victim, a 39-year-old woman, was taken to a hospital and was stable. Police didn’t release any details about a suspect.
story: A woman was sexually assaulted at knifepoint in New York City’s Central Park over the weekend, police said.
A man approached the 39-year-old victim near East 66th Street and Fifth Avenue on Saturday evening, displayed a knife and sexually assaulted her, the New York City Police Department said.
Police were called around 9:30 p.m., and the victim was taken to a hospital. She was stable.
For Subscribers
Police have not released a description of a suspect. No arrests have been made, and the investigation continues.
City Council Speaker Julie Menin condemned the attack on X, saying, “I am outraged by this horrific act of violence.”
For Subscribers

“My thoughts are with the survivor, and I hope she makes a full recovery,” Menin said. “Every New Yorker deserves to feel safe in our city. The perpetrator remains at large, but I have confidence that the NYPD will work swiftly to apprehend him and bring him to justice.”

The assault is the latest attack to occur in Central Park. Last week, a woman riding her bicycle through the park in the evening was attacked by three men, NBC New York reported. The men hit her in the head, and she fought back, she told police. One of them grabbed her bag before they fled. She sustained injuries to her face, neck and back.

title: Elvis Presley’s rights holders sue Anthropic, saying it trained AI on his music
summary: Anthropic has said it “disagree[s] with the claims and intend[s] to defend this case fully.”
story: The owners of Elvis Presley’s music have sued Anthropic, alleging it used his copyrighted lyrics without permission to train its AI models and generating infringing versions of his songs.

In a lawsuit filed Friday, Authentic Brands Group, the licensing platform that controls Presley’s intellectual property — along with other companies, trusts and individuals who own rights to his music — accused Anthropic of infringing copyrights to 274 songs without any license or payment.
These span some of Presley’s biggest hits, including “All Shook Up,” “Can’t Help Falling in Love,” “Don’t Be Cruel,” “A Little Less Conversation” and “Return to Sender.”
“The Elvis Plaintiffs’ iconic collective catalog contains some of the most groundbreaking, revolutionary, influential, and enduring musical compositions in human history,” the lawsuit stated.

The plaintiffs allege that the infringement has occurred throughout “the entire development” of Anthropic’s flagship Claude models and continues today as users generate outputs that reproduce copyrighted lyrics or create unauthorized adaptations of the songs.
“As we say in the lawsuit, the Elvis Plaintiffs are guardians of, and highly protective of, Elvis’s song which are some of the most iconic of all time,” attorney Richard Busch wrote in a statement.
A spokesperson for Anthropic wrote: “We disagree with the claims and intend to defend this case fully.”

The complaint further describes Anthropic as having “built its entire business model on infringing copyrights at an unfathomable scale,” pointing to the alleged mass scraping of internet content and pirating of books to develop its Claude language models.

Last year, Anthropic agreed to a landmark $1.5 billion settlement in a copyright infringement lawsuit filed by authors who alleged the company had illegally used pirated copies of their books to train AI models. It was the largest settlement in the history of American copyright cases.
The lawsuit by Presley’s rights holders comes amid a larger wave of lawsuits against Anthropic and other AI companies accused of using copyrighted musical works without consent or compensation.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers

In January, Universal Music, Concord Music Group and ABKCO Music expanded their lawsuit against Anthropic over the alleged infringement of copyrighted song lyrics. BMG Rights Management, Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Music filed similar lawsuits against Anthropic this year.

Anthropic and the AI music generation company Suno were also recently hit with lawsuits from the independent music publisher Round Hill — which is represented by Busch, the lead attorney for Presley’s rights holders — and the independent music company Reservoir Media.
“Even after the Defendant supposedly put up ‘guardrails’ after being sued, in one of its latest iterations, Claude continues to infringe,” the Presley rights holders state in their lawsuit.
The complaint notes that when asked recently to re-create specific songs “for a modern audience,” Claude did so.

“These renders keep landing very close to the originals: same structure, same hooks reused with light rewording, and full sets of verses/choruses/bridges,” the complaint said. “That’s edging past ‘inspired by’ into reproducing the copyrighted song, even when the words are swapped out.”
Presley’s rights holders are seeking $41.1 million in statutory copyright damages — up to $150,000 for each of the 274 works they alleged were willfully infringed — according to the complaint.
They also demand a permanent injunction to prevent Anthropic from “further infringing” on Presley’s works and an order for the company to destroy all unauthorized copies of the copyrighted works.

title: Mary Peltola delays campaign events after sustaining ‘minor injuries’ in car crash
summary: Anchorage police confirmed a crash involving three vehicles occurred Saturday and said those involved sustained “non-life threatening” injuries.
story: Former Rep. Mary Peltola is rescheduling several upcoming campaign events after she and her family sustained “minor” injuries in a car crash, her campaign announced Sunday.

“Mary and her family sustained minor injuries but are in good spirits. Unfortunately, per the advice of medical professionals, Mary’s upcoming events in Fairbanks and Bethel will be rescheduled for later in the week as she takes time to recover,” Peltola campaign manager Cheryl Bruce said in a statement.

“Mary is disappointed that the accident is delaying the start of her Alaska Always Tour, and she is eager to get back on the campaign trail to speak directly with Alaskans about her plan to take on the rigged system and lower costs for working families,” Bruce added.

Peltola was en route to the Alaska Federation of Natives’ annual banquet Saturday when a vehicle transporting the candidate and her family was struck by another driver, according to the campaign. A spokesperson for the campaign said they had no reason to believe the accident had been politically motivated.
The police department in Anchorage confirmed Sunday that a collision involving three vehicles occurred on evening and those involved sustained “non-life threatening injuries.”
Police added that the incident is under investigation.

Peltola, a Democrat, is locked in a competitive Senate race against GOP Sen. Dan Sullivan. She was elected to the House in 2022 but narrowly lost her re-election bid in 2024, the same year that President Donald Trump won the state by 13 percentage points.
Sullivan’s re-election race, in which he’s seeking a third term, is tighter than expected, with Alaska voters tying Trump to high gas and grocery prices resulting from the ongoing war with Iran.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Trump and Vice President JD Vance rallied voters in Alaska separately earlier this month.

Republicans have accused Democrats of recruiting another candidate named Dan Sullivan to run for the Senate, saying that voters may be confused by the presence of two Dan Sullivans on the ballot if they plan to vote for the incumbent senator.

Democrats have not taken credit for recruiting the second Dan Sullivan into the race. He’ll appear on the ballot as Dan J. Sullivan, while the incumbent senator will be identified by his name, political party and a clear notation that he’s the incumbent.

Last week, the Justice Department sued Alaska’s election officials, seeking to block certification of the election if Sen. Dan Sullivan loses. It cited Dan J. Sullivan’s presence on the ballot as a point of “voter confusion.”
On Saturday, Democrats filed a motion urging a federal judge to dismiss the case.

title: NFL fans visiting Paris in high spirits for Saints vs. Steelers game, undeterred by protests
summary: er people.
story: PARIS — American football fans brought high energy, chants and smiles to Stade de France on Sunday to watch the Pittsburgh Steelers face the New Orleans Saints. Some said the mass protests in the city were not an issue during their weekend trip.

The NFL’s first regular-season game in France came a day after more than 400,000 people around the country took to the streets to protest educational funding and the high cost of living. At least 110,000 of those protesters were concentrated in Paris, according to the French Interior Ministry.

Although the demonstrations were largely peaceful, some clashes broke out, prompting French security forces to use tear gas and water cannons in several cities. Paris prosecutors said there were 64 arrests in the nation’s capital on Saturday, mostly for suspected weapons offenses or participation in a group preparing violence or property damage.
But American visitors in town to cheer on their teams told NBC News that everyone they’ve encountered had been welcoming.

title: Cornell fraternity member seeks dismissal from Jane Doe’s sexual assault lawsuit
summary: An attorney for Diego Sarabia said his client isn’t accused of taking part in the alleged assault and should be excluded from the case.
story: One of the men sued by a former Cornell University student identified as Jane Doe has asked a judge to dismiss the claims against him, arguing that her allegations do not support her broader accusations of rape and sexual assault.

Diego Sarabia filed the motion Friday seeking dismissal of all claims against him in the lawsuit Doe filed Sept. 16 in New York state court. Sarabia, who was a member of the Chi Phi fraternity, was one of seven men originally sued by Doe for allegedly participating in a gang rape at the Chi Phi house from Oct. 19 to 20, 2024.

Sarabia denies the allegations against him, according to the filing. His attorneys argue that even if the complaint’s factual allegations are accepted as true for the purposes of the motion, the claims against him were filed too late, are legally insufficient, or both.

James C. Knox, an attorney for Sarabia, wrote in the motion that as far as the allegations against his client, “this is essentially a lawsuit about a forced kiss.” Knox argued that the conduct Doe attributed to Sarabia did not qualify for the extended statute of limitations she cited for certain sexual offenses.

Doe accused Sarabia of grabbing her face, kissing her and snorting ketamine off her body with other fraternity members during a drug- and alcohol-fueled encounter in what was known as the “alumni room” of the fraternity house.

“Throughout a sprawling complaint approaching 600 paragraphs, plaintiff repeatedly, collectively and without differentiation accuses seven student defendants of ‘sexual assault and rape,’” Knox wrote in his filing. “Those legally conclusory statements do not substitute for pleaded facts.”

Knox argued that the complaint did not allege that Sarabia “supplied her with drugs or alcohol, participated in any of the alleged sexual encounters described elsewhere in the complaint, or was even present for most of the conduct that forms the basis of plaintiff’s broader allegations.”

The attorney said that the assault, battery and intentional infliction of emotional distress claims were barred by a one-year statute of limitations and the allegations against Sarabia did not qualify for extensions cited in the complaint.
Doe’s attorney Thomas Giuffra declined to comment on Sunday. Giuffra previously agreed to withdraw claims against the acting president of the fraternity’s chapter at the time.

The lawsuit inspired calls for a reckoning at the Ivy League institution, where past and current students and community members have accused the administration of not doing enough to protect women from sexual assault.

Cornell’s Board of Trustees hired former Deputy Attorney General Sally Yates “to lead a comprehensive independent review of how the University prevents and responds to sexual harassment, sexual assault and related misconduct on campus.”

Doe’s allegations were investigated by Cornell University Police. An internal civil rights investigation led to the expulsion of two students and disciplinary action against others. Tompkins County District Attorney Matthew Van Houten declined to bring charges in November 2024 based on a six-page statement in which Doe described some of the sexual conduct that night as consensual.
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Van Houten declined to evaluate other investigative materials that had been gathered by investigators, including other witness statements.

Gov. Kathy Hochul called the evaluation inadequate and recently appointed state Attorney General Letitia James as special prosecutor to investigate the allegations. James’ office has started that process. The attorney general is expected to hire outside investigators to assist with the effort.

Two of the accused men are seeking to disqualify James from overseeing the investigation based on a comment she made on social media about the case before she was tapped to run the probe. They argued the state’s top law enforcement official had prejudged the case. Both challenges are still pending.
James has deflected calls to step down from the case and has said she is “committed to leading a comprehensive investigation they can trust, guided only by the facts, the evidence, and the law.”

title: Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer says America is ready to elect a woman
summary: The Michigan governor didn’t deny she’s exploring a run for president in 2028.
story: Michigan Gov. Gretchen Whitmer pushed back Sunday on comments made by former first lady Michelle Obama last year that U.S. voters aren’t ready to elect a female president.

“Listen, I have got a lot of colleagues who I think are probably interested in running for president, and I’ve heard everyone say, ‘You can’t have this person or that person,’” the governor told NBC News’ “Meet the Press.”

“I would put my money on any Democratic governor in the country against [Vice President] JD Vance or [Secretary of State] Marco Rubio in 2028,” she added, pointing to two Republicans widely expected to run for president in two years.
Asked directly whether a woman could be the best choice to beat a potential GOP presidential nominee in 2028, Whitmer simply said, “I do.”

In 2025, Obama said in public remarks: “As we saw in this past election, sadly, we ain’t ready. That’s why I’m like, don’t even look at me about running, because you all are lying. You’re not ready for a woman. You are not.”
Several women, including Whitmer and former Vice President Kamala Harris, are widely speculated to be potential candidates in the 2028 Democratic presidential primary.
On Sunday, Whitmer did not deny that she’s exploring a potential run for president in 2028, saying that she’ll decide on her next steps after she departs from her post as governor in January.

“When I exit office … I’m going to take a little time off and figure out what I want to do next, so I’ve got nothing new to share with you, unfortunately,” Whitmer told “Meet the Press” moderator Kristen Welker.
Earlier this year, Whitmer denied that she planned to run for president but quickly walked back the comments.
“There will be a robust group of people running for president,” she said at the time, adding, “I will not be one of them in 2028, I can tell you that.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Later the same day, the governor said: “I never thought I would run for governor. So I guess I should know better to never say never.”

Several other Democratic governors, including California Gov. Gavin Newsom, Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, Maryland Gov. Wes Moore and Pennsylvania Gov. Josh Shapiro, are also widely regarded as potential 2028 presidential candidates. Each has been crisscrossing the country ahead of the midterms campaigning on behalf of Democratic gubernatorial candidates in competitive races.
Whitmer on Sunday highlighted her support for former public health official Amy Acton, the Democratic nominee for governor in Ohio.

Earlier this week, Acton’s opponent, GOP businessman Vivek Ramaswamy, released a TV ad featuring Acton’s mother calling her a “liar.” Acton has publicly shared that she’s been estranged from her mother for nearly 50 years and has accused her late stepfather of sexually abusing her. Acton and her brother were removed from her mother’s custody in 1978 after her stepfather, Cledith Arthur, was arrested on a child rape charge. Acton’s mother has not responded to requests for comment.

“I’m going to stay focused on getting people like Amy Acton over the finish line. What’s happened to her in Ohio is absolutely abhorrent, and any survivor knows there’s always a backlash. But this is what makes it harder for women to seek help after they’ve been sexually assaulted in this country,” Whitmer said Sunday. “It is unreal what’s going on, and that’s why we’ve got to — we’ve got to win races like this and elect good people who are going to keep the people at the heart of their work, like Dr. Amy Acton.”
Ramaswamy’s decision to air the ad has faced widespread bipartisan condemnation, some of it from GOP Sen. Jon Husted of Ohio, who is locked in a tight re-election race.

title: Sen. Adam Schiff says Pete Hegseth should testify on Starlink slowdown in Ukraine
summary: The California Democrat said “anyone who has knowledge of what happened” with the Starlink slowdown should testify before the Senate.
story: Sen. Adam Schiff, D-Calif., told NBC’s “Meet the Press” on Sunday that Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth should testify before the Senate on the Starlink satellite limitations that disrupted Ukrainian military operations.
If Democrats retake the Senate, Schiff told “Meet the Press” moderator Kristen Welker, “Defense Secretary Hegseth should be brought in. Anyone who has knowledge of what happened.”

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on “Meet the Press” last week that the Ukrainian government believed the decision to limit Starlink came from the U.S. government. Zelenskyy said at the time that “it was the message from American government to limit this speed, and technically SpaceX did it.”
The Wall Street Journal reported last week that President Donald Trump called Musk and asked him to lift his company’s satellite service restrictions.

Ukraine said Saturday that Starlink and Starshield, its military network, were working at high speeds again. Last week, the systems were disrupted, and Ukraine said the disruptions made it harder to intercept incoming Russian attacks.

“You’ve got the president saying one thing, you’ve got Elon Musk saying another thing, you have them both saying different things at different times,” Schiff said. “Somebody is lying here. Maybe they’re all lying in different ways, but we need to find out.”

The disruptions to Starlink, which is run by Elon Musk’s SpaceX, led to rising tensions with the U.S. amid questions about who may have ordered the slowdown of the satellite services. Overnight, Musk accused Ukraine in posts to X of violating “Starlink terms of service” by using the system for offensive strikes. He said the “loophole was closed” and said that the company “simply enforced our terms of service when they were bypassed.”
Musk previously said that limits on “speed or usage” of Starshield are “decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS.”
For Subscribers
For Subscribers
Schiff said Sunday that “the world’s richest person shouldn’t be controlling our national security interests.”
“That is a spectacular threat to our national security,” he said. “If it is true, we should find out.”
Schiff referenced Musk’s overnight posts about Starlink’s policies, saying that “something changed within the last week.”

“What was it that changed?” Schiff said. “Why did it change? What impact is it having on Ukraine’s ability to defend itself? Is this in our national security interests? These are the questions we should ask, which frankly Republicans have been unwilling to ask.”

On Thursday, Trump said Musk restored Starlink in Ukraine. One day later, though, Ukraine denied that the satellite system was working properly. The Trump administration has denied that it requested changes to Starlink’s operation in Ukraine.

“The reporting out there was that somehow the United States government was denying them something they needed in order to defend their country,” Secretary of State Marco Rubio said last week. “That’s not true. That’s not accurate.”

title: Elon Musk says SpaceX closed Ukraine Starlink ‘loophole,’ while Kyiv denies breaching terms
summary: Musk called his critics “bloodthirsty warmongers” who “want the war to continue until every last man in Ukraine has died in a ditch.”
story: Elon Musk has said his company imposed limits on the use of its Starlink satellite system in Ukraine last week, after curbs led to disruption to Ukrainian military operations.

Ukraine said Saturday that both Starlink, run by Musk’s SpaceX, and its military variant Starshield were now fully functional after the long outage, two days after President Donald Trump indicated Musk had been asked to “put it back.”
In a series of posts on X on Saturday night into Sunday morning, Musk accused Ukraine of violating “Starlink terms of service” by using it for offensive drone strikes.
“That loophole was closed last week,” the billionaire wrote.
“Using Starlink, a civilian commercial service, for offensive drone strikes to kill people has never been allowed, nor should it be,” he added.
In a separate post, he said: “We simply enforced our terms of service when they were bypassed.”
SpaceX did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Neither Musk nor the United States government ​had initially taken responsibility for imposing the curbs last week, with Musk saying previously with respect to Starshield that “any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS.”
Trump says he 'wasn't involved' in limiting Ukraine's Starlink access
Starlink technology is critical to front-line communications as well as Ukraine’s drone operations and its ability to intercept jet-powered drones launched by Russia.

Ukrainian officials said the restrictions were imposed without warning and capped Starshield operations at speeds of 100 mph, hampering the military’s ability to intercept drones and forcing the cancellation of some operations.

“Starlink remains critical to the defense of Ukraine, as it is the only system that cannot be jammed or blown up, at least for now,” Musk said. “Were Starlink to be turned off, the Ukrainian front line would collapse immediately. This is NOT a threat, it is simply a statement of fact.”
In a series of posts and replies, he called his critics “bloodthirsty warmongers” who “want the war to continue until every last man in Ukraine has died in a ditch.”
Hours later, responding to an X user comment that said “Zelensky needs to go,” Musk responded: “Yes.”

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said Starlink speeds started returning to normal on Saturday night. Ukraine’s defense ministry said Saturday that the connection remained stable at over 250 mph. The Ukrainian military does not disclose the systems’ maximum operating speeds.
Russia has barraged Ukraine over the past week, Zelenskyy said on Sunday, though he did not draw any direct link to the limitations.

“This past week alone, Russia has launched around 1,600 guided aerial bombs, 48 missiles of various types, including ballistic missiles, and nearly 2,300 attack drones against Ukraine. Unfortunately, almost every day, these brutal strikes leave people killed and injured,” he said in a post on X.

title: Over 4 million tubes of toothpaste have been recalled, including several kids brands
summary: More than 4.3 million tubes of fluoride toothpaste, including Brush Buddies Hot Wheels, Crayola and My Little Pony, were recalled. Here’s how to check your tubes.
story: More than 4.3 million tubes of fluoride toothpaste — many of them kid-themed, in flavors like bubble gum, strawberry and watermelon — have been voluntarily recalled nationwide after the Food and Drug Administration flagged manufacturing problems at the facility that made them.

The recall covers several brands sold under licensed character names, along with a handful of lesser-known labels, and includes tubes with expiration dates stretching into mid-2028, meaning some of the affected toothpaste could be sitting in your medicine cabinet right now.

No illnesses or injuries have been reported. Still, the FDA says families should check lot numbers and expiration dates to see whether their toothpaste is part of the recall. Below, I break down exactly which products are affected, how to tell if you have one and what to do next.
Why were more than 4 million tubes of toothpaste recalled?

The FDA announced the recall of more than 4.3 million tubes of fluoride toothpaste distributed nationwide because of current good manufacturing practice deviations. Those are federal standards meant to ensure products are made consistently and safely, so a deviation means the manufacturing process didn’t meet requirements, not necessarily that the toothpaste itself is harmful.

The voluntary recall was initiated on September 10 by Pritam International Private Limited, an India-based manufacturer, and the FDA classified it as Class II recall on October 19. A Class II recall is for products that could cause temporary or medically reversible health problems, where the chance of serious harm is considered unlikely. The FDA notice did not report any illnesses or injuries linked to the recalled toothpaste.

Many of the affected tubes were marketed to kids. The recalled products include toothpaste sold under the Brush Buddies, Crayola, Hot Wheels and My Little Pony brands, in flavors such as bubble gum, strawberry, watermelon, peppermint, sweet mint and cool mint. They were distributed by Ashtel Studios Inc. of Ontario, California, and come in 3.5-ounce and 4-ounce tubes, plus a two-pack of 3.5-ounce tubes.

Affected products carry expiration dates from November 2026 through June 2028, and consumers should check the lot numbers and expiration dates on the FDA’s recall notice to see whether theirs is included.
What to do if you have the recalled toothpaste

The FDA’s recall notice doesn’t include specific instructions for consumers, and neither the manufacturer nor the distributor has issued public guidance on returns or refunds. Until they do, the safest move is to stop using the toothpaste immediately and toss it out. Start by checking the brand, lot number and expiration date on your tube against the FDA’s recall notice; if it matches, discard it and switch to a different fluoride toothpaste so your family’s brushing routine isn’t interrupted.

Hang on to your receipt or take a photo of the packaging before tossing it, in case a refund process is announced later. No illnesses or injuries have been reported, but if you or your child used the product and have any concerns, you should contact your dentist or doctor immediately.
Other toothpastes to use instead
The below toothpastes were not recalled and have at least a four-star average rating from thousands of customers.

My kids absolutely love this toothpaste — in fact, it is the only one they will use. The fruity flavor makes brushing less of a chore, while fluoride fights cavities and calcium and silica gently clean teeth. It’s approved by the American Dental Association (ADA), free of artificial colors, flavors, and preservatives, and suitable for children ages 2 and up.

This toothpaste’s bright blue, sparkly color will delight kids. Plus, the fluoride formula fights cavities while staying gentle on enamel, and it carries the ADA Seal of Acceptance. It is suitable for children ages 2 and up, with adult supervision.

If you can’t decide on which hello kids’ flavor your little one will love, grab this variety pack that lets them sample all three and pick a favorite. Each toothpaste comes in a brightly colored tube with an easy flip cap that sits flat when closed, so it stands neatly on the bathroom counter.

If you had one of the adult toothpastes in the recall, Crest Pro-Health Advanced is a reliable replacement from a brand you already know. It’s an antibacterial fluoride toothpaste that fights plaque bacteria and supports healthy gums. It also helps whiten teeth and strengthen enamel.

title: Woman sexually assaulted at knifepoint in Central Park, police say
summary: The victim, a 39-year-old woman, was taken to a hospital and was stable. Police didn’t release any details about a suspect.

Police were called around 9:30 p.m., and the victim was taken to a hospital. She was stable.
For Subscribers
Police have not released a description of a suspect. No arrests have been made, and the investigation continues.
City Council Speaker Julie Menin condemned the attack on X, saying, “I am outraged by this horrific act of violence.”
For Subscribers

“My thoughts are with the survivor, and I hope she makes a full recovery,” Menin said. “Every New Yorker deserves to feel safe in our city. The perpetrator remains at large, but I have confidence that the NYPD will work swiftly to apprehend him and bring him to justice.”

The assault is the latest attack to occur in Central Park. Last week, a woman riding her bicycle through the park in the evening was attacked by three men, NBC New York reported. The men hit her in the head, and she fought back, she told police. One of them grabbed her bag before they fled. She sustained injuries to her face, neck and back.

title: As ‘Hey Arnold’ Turns 30, Its Creator Reflects On Show’s Portrayal of Real, Raw Topics
summary: As fans wrap their minds around the show’s 30th anniversary in October, creator Craig Bartlett is reflecting on the enduring love for “Hey Arnold!,” particularly for the cartoon’s refusal to shy away from the raw and real.
story: Between its iconic jazzy saxophone intro music, the wacky personalities at P.S. 118 and Football Head’s teenage dream of a bedroom, “Hey Arnold!” has charmed millennials for decades, uniting 90s kids of all backgrounds.

But ask anyone for the most memorable part of the Nickelodeon program and they’ll likely point to the show’s depth — the episodes that bore into loss, the struggle to fit in and the undeniable complexity of childhood.

As fans wrap their minds around the show’s 30th anniversary in October, creator Craig Bartlett is reflecting on the enduring love for “Hey Arnold!,” particularly for the cartoon’s refusal to shy away from the raw and real. Bartlett tells TODAY.com that it’s all been rewarding as that’s exactly what the show set out to do.

“You know, everyone was trying to figure out how to make their cartoon have its own unique corner, where it was different from everything else,” Bartlett says. “And for me, it was emotional authenticity.”

Anchored around friendly fourth-grader Arnold Shortman, the show, which premiered on October 7, 1996, ran for five seasons across nearly eight years. While the program had no shortage of laughs, it was the cartoon’s handling of issues like depression, addiction, poverty and more that, many viewers say, made it stand out.

Episode “Arnold’s Christmas” from Season 1, for example, looks into the backstory of character Mr. Hyunh, who, it’s revealed, is a refugee who was tragically separated from his infant daughter amid the Fall of Saigon, the historic event that marked the end of the Vietnam War.

In another episode later on in the series, character Chocolate Boy attempts to get over his addiction to chocolate. As Arnold helps him throughout his journey, Chocolate Boy reveals that his attachment to the candy stems from a beloved nanny he had when he was young, who gave him a bag of chocolate upon her departure from the family.

And who could forget the episode in which the gruff and tough Helga sits down with a school psychologist. It’s through the therapy sessions that it’s revealed that under her hard exterior is a girl from a dysfunctional household who’s felt largely forgotten by her parents. Helga’s obsession with Arnold, the episode shows, goes back to a moment on her first day of preschool. While her parents paid her no mind, leaving her to walk alone in the rain, Arnold, it turns out, is the first to notice Helga that day and display any semblance of kindness to her.

The showrunner explains that the franchise actually started off as claymation shorts that appeared on “Sesame Street.” In those shorts, Arnold was five years old. But Bartlett “grew him up” for Nickelodeon, he says.

“He was meant to be like me when I was little, and I was kind of bored with everything, and a daydreamer that was not present in some ways,” Bartlett says. “By the time we got him into growing him up into ‘Hey Arnold!’ he was a fourth grader who did things with friends, but he still was a dreamer — you’d imagine he had a real kind of freeform imagination, and that was how it started.”

Bartlett says that much of his inspiration was drawn from the 1965 animated classic “A Charlie Brown Christmas.” In it, main character Charlie Brown fails to feel the holiday cheer, despite the warmth and celebration of the season. Bartlett says that the film’s acknowledgement of its main character’s melancholy was deeply comforting to him as a kid.
“I was so affected by ‘Charlie Brown Christmas’ — that he was bummed and he knew he was supposed to love Christmas and be happy, but it wasn’t there,” Bartlett explains.
It’s reflective, he adds, of the sense of “yearning” often felt in those younger years.
“That describes childhood to me. You’re … hoping for cool things, and not necessarily having it,” he says “That, I think, was really key. It was what I was trying to convey.”

Bartlett says that as he created the show, he aimed to reflect some of those heavier emotions that children naturally feel. While many of the topics that were told through the eyes of the show’s characters were often serious in nature, Bartlett explains that he and his staff weren’t worried about whether kids would get it.
“We trusted that kids were living lives like that,” Bartlett says, raising Helga’s story as an example. “Some were living lives like they felt unseen like Helga.”

The show was also one of the first cartoons to feature kids voicing kids. And the young, tween actors at the time who provided the oh-so-memorable voices of the cast, from Lane Toran as Arnold to Francesca Marie Smith as Helga, also inspired much of the writing and injected personality into the characters, Bartlett says.
The storylines weren’t the only aspect that gave the show its authentic feel. Bartlett says that the music from composer Jim Lang was essential to conveying the show’s raw emotions.

“The music went hand in hand. Jim took all those ideas and turned them into really good, bummed-out music,” Bartlett says. “It’s about being bummed. And I just thought Jim, he really intensified that feeling. I can’t picture those episodes without the music.”

Bartlett adds that the freedom that the crew had to experiment with themes and storylines played a big part in bringing those meaningful lessons on screen. At the time, Bartlett says, Nickelodeon essentially gave the group free-reign to play.
“It’s hard to believe that the network let us operate that way, but they did. They just left us alone, mostly to do our thing,” he says.
The moment, he says, was perfect.

“You really got the vibe it was time for us to do our own thing, and that they were really going to let us do it,” he says.  “It was just such good times for everybody. Nick was making tons of money, and so they were like, ‘If it ain’t broke, don’t fix.’”

While the show ended in 2004, it got one final curtain call with the 2017 television flick, “Hey Arnold: The Jungle Movie.” Since then, there’s been no shortage of love for the show. Lang has even taken the music back on the road with project PS 118 All Stars, in which the band behind the iconic songs plays the tracks live for audiences across the U.S. Bartlett is a special guest for many of the dates.
Though fans have long called for a “Hey Arnold!” revival, Bartlett says he isn’t certain whether there will be anymore Arnold Shortman stories on our future screens.
For now, he says he’s happy to be joining shows as part of the PS 118 All Stars, comparing the tour experience to that of Mr. Hyunh in the episode “Mr. Hyunh Goes Country.”
“I’m super grateful I got to do 100 half-hours and two movies eventually,” Bartlett says. “If there’s no more Arnold TV or movies, I’m glad that it ended so, so nicely.”

title: Sister of ‘Breaking Bad’ Star RJ Mitte Shares Heartbreaking Instagram Tribute to Late Actor
summary: Lacianne Carriere, sister of “Breaking Bad” star RJ Mitte, shared some heartbreaking reflections on the actor’s passing.
story: Lacianne Carriere, sister of “Breaking Bad” star RJ Mitte, shared some heartbreaking reflections on the actor’s passing.
Carriere posted an emotional tribute on Instagram Oct. 24, detailing her grief after Mitte died by suicide earlier this month. He was 34.
In the open letter to her brother, Carriere expressed the shock she experienced when she received the news of his death.

“There are just no words. You were just here.. your strawberry Fanta was still sitting on my coffee table when I got the call,” Carriere wrote in the post. “Life hasn’t felt real since then..Rj you were my everything. I just lost my other half.”

Mitte, best known for playing his role as Walter “Flynn” White Jr. on “Breaking Bad,” was also a philanthropist and disability rights advocate. He died in Brownsville, Texas, where lived, the Brownsville Justice of the Peace confirmed.
In Carriere’s post, which included several throwback pictures of the siblings in addition to some sweet videos of Mitte, she detailed the immense impact that the actor had on her life.

“Every single aspect of my personality is because of your influence,” Carriere wrote. “My music taste, my film taste the video games I love… because of you I am a collector, you taught me that even the smallest piece of paper can be a precious memory later on.”
She also shared that since Mitte’s death, she’s been “sitting around with your closest people,” reminiscing on the “craziest stories that could never be said anywhere else.”

“you were the life of the party, coolest guy that we all tried to keep up with but never could. You made me, me,” she wrote. “We had so much more to do, so many more memories to be shared and I don’t know if my heart can ever be whole again after losing the biggest piece of it.”
Carriere also opened up about her struggles with her grief.

“I just really need my brother right now…You would put on some lofi music and tell me to get up and go sit in the shower, how it always makes you feel better,” she wrote. “I know you’re telling me right now that I’ll be okay though I don’t know how I will. But I promise I’m going to do my hardest and I promise your love will always live through me until the day I see you again.”
She ended the post with a quote from the 2018 miniseries “The Haunting of Hill House.”
“I loved you completely,” she wrote. “And you loved me the same. That’s all. The rest is confetti. 💜”

Mitte’s death came as a shock to many, including his family. His mother Dyna Carriere told NBC News that the actor had no history of mental illness and never saw a therapist. He had been going through a difficult emotional time recently, but he made no indication that he might end his life, she said.
“For the last three months, I’d been offering for him to go to therapy, trying to get him to go there, but he was like, ‘No, I’ve got it. It’s OK. I’m handling it,’” she told NBC News.

title: Heidi Klum, Halloween Queen, Just Shared A Hint For Her Upcoming Costume
summary: Model and television personality Heidi Klum, who’s known for her yearly over-the-top Halloween costumes and annual bash, shared a post on Instagram Oct. 24, teasing her get-up for the occasion.
story: The queen of Halloween has bestowed upon us a hint!

Model and television personality Heidi Klum, who’s known for her yearly over-the-top Halloween costumes and annual bash, shared a post on Instagram Oct. 24, teasing her get-up for the upcoming occasion.
The photo, a close-up shot of the costume, could be ...anything!
“What’s my costume?🤪” Klum, 53, wrote in the caption. “One week to go…. 🫆🔎👻🎃🧛🏻‍♀️😱🩸🦇🕸️ #HeidiHalloween”
The photo features what appears to be different material covered in a glossy gel. There’s a bit that resembles pink brains while another portion looks like small, yellowish craters.
It’s a head-scratcher.

Fans have been making their share of costume guesses, ranging from a coral reef to internal organs. A few social media users theorized that Klum could be a mushroom zombie from HBO series “The Last of Us.”

Whatever Klum’s costume is, we’re almost certain that the look will wow us. The supermodel has stunned fans with outrageous looks throughout the years at her big, annual Halloween bash. Some of her standout costumes, which often involve her husband Tom Kaulitz, include an enormous worm and E.T.

Klum told The Hollywood Reporter that her love for costumes came from her upbringing in Germany. Each year, the region’s festival Karneval prompts a host of festivities including vibrant costumes and lots of partying. But unlike Halloween, there isn’t a scary element to the celebrations.

“When I moved to America, I immediately fell in love with Halloween and the spookiness of it,” Klum told the outlet in a 2018 interview. “All that was missing was a fantastic party. It felt like a real opportunity for me.”

title: Paris Hilton Recreates Iconic Britney Spears VMAs Outfit For Halloween, Live Snake and All.
summary: For Halloween, Paris Hilton recreated the pop princess Britney Spears’ legendary look from her 2001 performance at the MTV Video Music Awards.
story: Socialite and businesswoman Paris Hilton’s Halloween costume is totally #Sliving.

Hilton recreated the pop princess Britney Spears’ legendary look from her 2001 performance at the MTV Video Music Awards. And the reality star, who revealed the costume on Oct. 23, simply nailed the ensemble — down to the live yellow snake.

“I always had the utmost respect for Brittany, but the fact that she performed at the VMAs with one of these around her neck is the most legendary thing that I’ve ever heard of my life,” Hilton said in a behind-the-scenes video shared on Instagram. “Especially after experiencing it just in the hallway of my house, I can’t imagine being on stage performing in front of thousands of people with this around my shoulders. That is badass. I love you, Brit.”

To recreate the look, Hilton rocked a green top, disco shorts that featured a blue and green ombré butterfly print and a bedazzled belt with shimmering, rhinestone tassels. She also posed with a snake named Tango around her neck, just as the daring pop star did during that iconic 2001 performance of “I’m a Slave 4 U.” In the behind-the-scenes video, Tango’s handler shared that the snake weighs roughly 30-40 lbs.
Now, that’s commitment.
Spears’ VMAs performance at New York City’s Metropolitan Opera house has become the stuff of legend in the two decades that have passed since she famously donned a yellow snake around her neck.

During the act, Spears, then 19, begins the routine inside a cage with a live tiger. Wearing a costume created by designers Kurt Swanson and Bart Mueller, Spears, giving some real jungle vibes, performs the striking act before ending it with Banana, the python.

Since, the performance has been praised as one of the most memorable moments in the VMAs’ over 40-year history. And plenty of people have referenced Spears’ daring act. In 2001, actor Elle Fanning also recreated the look for Halloween.
Actor Elle Fanning recreated the look as well for Halloween in 2021. She pulled it off flawlessly — even if the snake was fake.

title: Janet Jackson Makes Rare Public Appearance In An Outfit That’s ‘Nasty’ In The Best Way
summary: Pop icon Janet Jackson, 60, stepped out for a rare public appearance at the Dancers Against Cancer’s Gala of the Stars on Oct. 22 in Beverly Hills. Jackson, who presented an award to rapper Missy Elliott later on in the night, shut down the red carpet with her absolutely nasty look.
story: Ms. Jackson has entered the building.

Pop icon Janet Jackson, 60, stepped out for a rare public appearance at Dancers Against Cancer’s Gala of the Stars on Oct. 22 in Beverly Hills. Jackson, who presented an award to rapper Missy Elliott later on in the night, shut down the red carpet with her absolutely nasty look.
“Janet is ageless! That dress is stunning!” one social media user wrote on platform Threads.
Jackson’s ensemble featured a black lace, custom Christian Siriano gown. The dress included long sleeves and a peplum skirt around the hips. She completed the look with an elegant slicked-back ‘do.
The look received praise across the internet, including from a couple of style icons in their own right.
“Major,” celebrity stylist Law Roach commented under a photo of the pop god.

Jackson’s appearance was part of a star-studded event that aimed to raise funds to help support dancers, choreographers and their families amid battles with cancer. The event, hosted by “Dancing With The Stars” alum Maksim Chmerkovskiy, honored a number of big names in dance, including Toni Basil, Hilaria Baldwin, Vincent Paterson and the late Chita Rivera.

Jackson introduced honoree Missy Elliott before presenting the “Work It” rapper with the Icon Award. In her heartfelt speech, Jackson described the rapper, who’s long been known for imaginative dance routines in music videos and performances, as someone who “elevated choreography, embraced individuality, and inspired generations of dancers to dream bigger.”

“That influence lives far beyond a single song or a single performance,” Jackson said in the speech, which received tremendous applause. “It lives in every artist who feels a little braver because Missy showed them what was possible.”
Elliott later shared a heartfelt post about her friend Jackson.

“Dear @janetjackson we have been friends way over two decades, & I still am one of your BIGGEST fans! Of course, I’m a fan of your music, BUT I’m the biggest fan of YOU, the PERSON!” Elliott wrote in the emotional Instagram post. “With all that you’ve done globally, you have NEVER been loudest in the room, but those in the room know you are MOTHA! Your SELFLESSNESS & HUMILITY should be studied! Your beauty outside matches the INSIDE!”
Elliott concluded by expressing her love for Jackson.
“I Love you, j, & thank you for this award it’s the best feeling getting a ICON award from a ICON!” she wrote.

title: Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders Take Legal Action Against Band My Chemical Romance
summary: The parent company of the famed cheerleading squad the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have filed a temporary restraining order against popular rock band My Chemical Romance over a costume dispute.
story: The parent company of the famed cheerleading squad the Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders have filed a temporary restraining order against popular rock band My Chemical Romance over a costume dispute.

Pro Silver Star, the owner of the high-profile cheerleading squad’s brand, filed a motion Oct. 23, seeking a temporary restraining order to bar the “Welcome to the Black Parade” band from using the squad’s iconic costumes on stage.

It comes after the band’s recent performances at the Hollywood Bowl in Los Angeles featured dancers in what appeared to be Dallas Cowboys Cheerleaders-inspired outfits. In their court filing, Pro Silver Star argued that the use of the outfits weren’t authorized.

In the legal filing, the company said that it takes “no issue” with the band’s music, nor is it looking for the defendants to change their choreography or “even their decision to put gun-toting performers on stage.”
“Silver Star asks only that those performers not wear the DCC Uniform while doing it,” the company said in the filing. “The universe of alternative costume designs is effectively unlimited.”
My Chemical Romance did not immediately respond to TODAY.com’s request for comment.
Pro Silver Star is also seeking a preliminary injunction on the use of the costumes, according to the motion that was filed in the District Court of Dallas County.

In the document, Pro Silver Star alleges that during the band’s opening night at the Hollywood Bowl on Oct. 21, the rock group had a line of female dancers, dressed as the DCC cheerleaders, to perform a choreographed routine during the hit song “Teenagers.” The “counterfeit uniforms” reflected the “signature elements” of the DCC outfit, from the white boots to the white vest with blue stars.
Fan videos from the night show the performers, holding blue-and-white pom-poms, dancing in unison to the hit 2006 single.
The filing then says that the costumed performers were handed rifles and joined in a staged firefight before then “depicted being shot and crawling off the stage.”

“The brand DCC built on dedication, character, and community, and on decades of entertaining American troops, was thus put on a stage in a gunfight, its uniform worn by performers shown shooting and being shot,” the filing said.

My Chemical Romance has long been a staple in the alt rock scene and counter culture movements. Climbing the charts in the 2000s with emo hits like “Helena” the band hit the peak of its commercial success with 2006 album “The Black Parade.” The band’s shows at the Hollywood Bowl are part of a 20th anniversary tour in celebration of the album. The band will perform again at the iconic venue on Oct. 24.

title: Prince William Reveals He Went Through a DJ Phase — and Even Had A Stage Name
summary: Prince William, who joined the Oct. 23 episode of “The Graham Norton Show,” opened up about how he once aspired to be a DJ in his younger years. And he even had a stage name.
story: Prince William could’ve been the king of the club.
The 44-year-old royal, who joined the Oct. 23 episode of “The Graham Norton Show,” opened up about how he once aspired to be a DJ in his younger years. And he even had a stage name.
“I went through a phase where I wanted to be a DJ, which didn’t go very well,” the prince said, laughing. “And I came up with a name. It was called DJ Xara with an X. It wasn’t good.”

William — who joined the longtime British talk show alongside fellow guests Cate Blanchett, Hannah Waddingham and Robert Irwin — acknowledged that as a child, he did, in fact, fantasize about going into a non-royal profession.
William told host Graham Norton that at one point, he thought about perhaps becoming a police officer.
“Being a policeman, I thought was quite cool,” William said.
Then came the DJ phase, William explained. Unfortunately, the Prince of Wales never got to play any gigs. When asked if he ever DJ’d any school parties, the prince gave an honest answer.
“No, I didn’t,” William said, smiling. “I never got that good.”

Prince William, the heir apparent to the British throne, may not be in the DJ booth these days, but he appears to be pretty busy, working on charitable projects and carrying out his official royal duties. Some of his main causes include the environment, homelessness and the armed forces.

He does, of course, have down time, which he fills with some good ‘ol reality TV. Prince William told Norton that he and his children are big fans of “The Celebrity Traitors,” hosted by broadcaster Claudia Winkleman.
“I love it. The family love it,” he said of the show. “Charlotte and Louis are obsessed with it. It’s really good telly.”

title: Alfonso Ribeiro Shares Why He Was Nervous to Dance With Tatyana Ali on ‘Dancing With the Stars’
summary: Alfonso Ribeiro tells TODAY.com about how he felt nervous to perform with Tatyana Ali during “Dancing With the Stars” Dedication Night.
story: Dedication Night on “Dancing With the Stars” is the episode that pulls at the heartstrings, and this year was no different. It was also the night that made co-host Alfonso Ribeiro the most “nervous.”

During the Oct. 20 episode, Tatyana Ali honored the late James Avery. The “Fresh Prince of Bel-Air” star and partner Jan Ravnik danced a Viennese waltz to “(You Don’t Know) How Glad I Am” by Nancy Wilson.
Already an emotional number, it became extra heartwarming when Ali was joined by Ribeiro, who stepped in midway and replaced Ravnik.

“It was nice. It was the first time I’ve actually felt nervous. Even my whole season, I never felt nervous,” Ribeiro, who won Season 19 of “DWTS,” tells TODAY.com. “But I was nervous because I wanted to be great for her, for James Avery. It wasn’t about me.”

Ali and Ribeiro worked alongside Avery for six seasons of the sitcom from 1990 to 1996. They portrayed siblings, Ashley and Carlton Banks, while Avery was the ever-wise, stern, yet softie dad Philip Banks. Avery died Dec. 31, 2013 at the age of 68.
For the performance, Ali waltzed around the ballroom floor with Ravnik before she and Ribeiro continued the routine in synchronized steps.
At the conclusion of the tribute, they held hands and a photo of a smiling Avery appeared on the screen. They turned to face their former TV dad, before embracing.
Ribeiro says he wanted to make the moment great for Ali, which meant making sure he didn’t miss a beat.

“When I was competing on the show ... if I mess up, I cause harm to myself ... but I had to lead Tatyana,” he says. “I had to be the one during that part of the routine where I’m taking the place of Jan and I’m actually having to lead in that dance — a dance that I never did before.”

Ribeiro, who won with pro Witney Carson, says he never tackled the Viennese waltz. Despite the additional challenge, he says, “It was so wonderful to be a part of that. I felt incredibly honored to be asked to be a part of their number and to represent James Avery.”
He notes that as co-host of “DWTS,” he takes “being neutral to all of the contestants very seriously.” However, he didn’t want to pass up this opportunity.

“But this was special because it was James Avery. James played my dad on three different sitcoms,” he says, referring to 1995’s “In the House” and the short-lived “Things We Do for Love.” “It was very special to be able to do that for him, and it was nice to be able to collaborate with Jan and with Tatyana on what the story was going to be, and it was beautiful.”
The “America’s Funniest Home Videos” host also noted that Ross Bagley, who played Nicky Banks on “Fresh Prince,” was in attendance that night, as well.
When asked if he and Ali had heard from Avery’s family following the dedication, he says yes.
“There was a text chain with all of us, and basically everyone was like, ‘Beautifully said. Beautifully done. James would be very proud,’” he shares. “So it felt good.”

title: Prince William Shares the Reality Show Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis Are ‘Obsessed With’
summary: Prince William revealed that a reality television show that has quickly become a global phenomenon has also captured the attention of Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis.
story: Prince William has revealed that a reality television show that has quickly become a global phenomenon has also captured the attention of the royal family.

The Prince of Wales made a surprise appearance on Britain’s “The Graham Norton Show” Oct. 23 and opened up about some of his favorite pastimes. While sitting on the couch next to fellow celebrity guests Cate Blanchett, Hannah Waddingham and Robert Irwin, Prince William told host Graham Norton that his family are big fans of “The Celebrity Traitors.”
“I love it. The family love it. Charlotte and Louis are obsessed with it. It’s really good telly,” he praised.
U.K. series “Celebrity Traitors,” hosted by Claudia Winkleman, began airing its second season on Oct. 1. Prince William said he recently tried to re-create a moment from the season premiere.

“I saw Ross Kemp the day after the first episode and I couldn’t help but try — in the most appropriate way – to touch him to see what reaction I got from him. Turns out he was really jumpy!” he marveled.

Kemp, a reporter, went viral after the first episode for his paranoia. He wondered if singer and Little Mix star Leigh-Anne Pinnock might be a Traitor after she lightly tapped his shoulder while walking around the castle.
In addition to Pinnock and Kemp, the cast this season also features Richard E. Grant, Michael Sheen and Miranda Hart.
During his time on “The Graham Norton Show,” Prince William shared other ways he likes to unwind.
“It is music and film. I love getting immersed in deep-thinking films. I like action films too, but I like something a bit different,” he said.
The British royal revealed he is a huge fan of Christopher Nolan.

“His films are fantastic — ‘The Dark Knight’ series is psychologically dark and deep and I absolutely love that. He takes concepts that are completely out there and makes them incredibly entertaining,” he gushed.
The royal family supports some of their favorite Hollywood stars from time to time at public events.
In September, the prince and his wife, Catherine, Princess of Wales, attended the world premiere of “Digger” in London. They were photographed chatting with star Tom Cruise on the red carpet.

title: The Sarah J. Maas Universe: How ‘ACOTAR,’ ‘Crescent City’ and ‘Throne of Glass’ Are Connected
summary: Before “A Court of Splintered Harmony,” revisit how Sarah J. Maas’ three series - “ACOTAR,” “Crescent City” and “Throne of Glass” - are connected in one universe.
story: 🚨 Spoilers ahead for Sarah J. Maas’ book series “Throne of Glass,” “A Court of Thorns and Roses” and “Crescent City.”
Before Sarah J. Maas releases the next novel in her “A Court of Thorns and Roses” series, many readers are revisiting the last story in which those characters appeared.
The only tricky element? That story was not a “Court of Thorns and Roses” book.

“A Court of Silver Flames” from 2021 is indeed the most recent book published in the “ACOTAR” series, but — and here comes the spoiler — some of those characters were last seen on the page in another series written by Maas: “Crescent City’s” third book from 2024, “House of Flame and Shadow.” That 850-page behemoth was the first to give a fuller scope at how all three of Maas’ fantasy series — “ACOTAR,” “Crescent City” and “Throne of Glass” — intertwine in one larger universe.
Here’s a deep dive into all the Easter eggs, callbacks and references that connect the three book series, ranging from the cryptic to the overt.
More on Sarah J. Maas

How ‘ACOTAR’ and ‘Throne of Glass’ Connect
The first explicit crossover between Maas’ series came in 2018, with the “Throne of Glass” finale, “Kingdom of Ash.”

As Aelin falls between worlds at the peak of her battle with the Valg, she passes through a “world of snowcapped mountains under shining stars” and sees two Fae: one winged male and one “heavily pregnant female.” The male notices her falling and sends his power, “like a gentle summer night,” to slow her down. This is Rhysand and Feyre, likely during the events of “A Court of Silver Flames,” which lines up with her pregnancy.

When “A Court of Silver Flames” published in 2021, some readers believed that moment was seen from the other perspective. In Chapter 62, after the annual Starfall event, a “rare red star” is spotted blasting across the sky and is interpreted as an “ill omen.”
How ‘ACOTAR’ and ‘Crescent City’ Connect
“Crescent City” more clearly establishes that the worlds of Maas’ three series are interconnected, starting with last line of the last chapter in Book 2, “House of Sky and Breath.”

At the end of “Crescent City” 2, heroine Bryce Quinlan confronts the Asteri, the rulers of her planet, Midgard. She learns they are not benevolent leaders but parasites who survive on firstlight generated by magical beings. When she learns the truth, she tries to use the Horn, which can open rifts between worlds, to go to Hel for help against the Asteri.

Instead she lands in another world, surrounded by Fae who believe her to be a threat. One of them looks eerily similar to her brother, Ruhn. When Bryce says her name, that Fae male responds: “Hello, Bryce Quinlan. My name is Rhysand.”
And there ends Book 2.

Book 3, “House of Flame and Shadow,” picks up where Book 2 leaves off. When Bryce lands in Prythian, Rhys and his Inner Circle interrogate Bryce. Soon they all learn that the Asteri, the primary villains in “Crescent City,” are the same as the Daglan, an evil force found in the history books of Prythian.

Readers learn in “A Court of Silver Flames” that the Daglan were vanquished by Rhys’ ancestors 15,000 years before the events of the books. But in “House of Flame and Shadow,” Bryce discovers that the Daglan escaped to Midgard to conquer a new planet and curate sources of power to serve as food. But they have maintained a desire to find a way back to their home world.

The ancient Fae relic known as the Horn is a big part of “Crescent City” lore. It’s first introduced in “House of Earth and Blood” when it goes missing from its place in Luna’s Temple. By the end of the book, readers learn Bryce’s best friend, Danika, had discovered the Horn’s ability to open doors between worlds, ground it into ashes, mixed it with ink and imbued it onto Bryce’s back as a tattoo when she was drunk. This was Danika’s effort to hide the Horn from the evil people looking for it and happened days before she was killed.

While Bryce is in Prythian in “House of Flame and Shadow,” she learns that the Horn is actually part of the Dread Trove, a collection of powerful artifacts made by the Cauldron. In a “Court of Silver Flames,” Nesta and the Night Court find the other three relics in the Trove — the Harp, the Crown and the Mask.

And speaking of missing artifacts — Bryce and the Night Court crew also learn in “House of Flame and Shadow” that Gwydion, a long-missing sword that’s a pair to spymaster Azriel’s dagger Truth-Teller, is none other than Bryce’s Starsword, a weapon in Midgard that can only be wielded by the chosen Starborn Fae.

In “House of Flame and Shadow,” Bryce at first tries to hide from the Night Court crew her tattoo that contains the Horn. The tattoo is written in a script Bryce doesn’t even know and is supposed to translate to, “Through love, all is possible.”

Amren is first to clock the tattoo and tells Rhys that Bryce’s tattoo is written in the same language found in “The Book of Breathings,” an object in the “ACOTAR” world with an ability to control the Cauldron. The book is also mysteriously mentioned in “House of Earth and Blood”; it’s in Jesiba Roga’s library alongside “The Walking Dead,” a book from “Throne of Glass.”

In “A Court of Mist and Fury,” Amren identifies the language in which “The Book of Breathings” is written as “Leshon Kadoesh” or “The Holy Tongue.” Rhys then shares that, according to legend, the language is one “of mighty beings who were here ... and then vanished.”

In “House of Flame and Shadow,” Bryce teams up with Nesta and Azriel to navigate a tunnel system near the Prison, led by the light from the glowing eight-pointed star on Bryce’s chest. One of the obstacles they face is the Middengard Wyrm, a large-toothed monster that Feyre faces in the first “ACOTAR” book.
But Bryce raises an interesting question when facing the creature.
“Middengard? Like — Midgard? Did they come from my world originally?” she asks, though Nesta and Azriel are unable to answer.

The theory of a lost Dusk Court was popular among “ACOTAR” fans, since it felt like a glaring omission from Prythian’s landscape. The continent has four seasonal courts — Spring, Autumn, Summer and Winter — and three solar courts — Night, Day and Dawn, but no Dusk.
It turns, it did once exist.

In “House of Flame and Shadow,” Bryce, Azriel and Nesta end up in the Prison via the tunnel system and find the same spot Nesta had found the Harp in “A Court of Silver Flames.” (The Harp was notably found on top of a “large rendering of an eight-pointed star.”) (Notably, Nesta has an eight-pointed star on her spine, and Bryce has one that glows on her chest.) (Also notably, a High Priestess in “Throne of Glass” has an eight-pointed star tattooed on her forehead.)

The three then encounter a hologram of Silene, the long lost daughter of Theia, a Fae queen and the original Starborn. Though Bryce already knew she is a descendent of Theia, Silene’s storytelling is how she learns that the Starborn Fae of Midgard had originated in Prythian.

According to Silene, Theia had served the Daglan for a long time while in Prythian, but eventually overthrew them and was able to claim her land — the island on which the Prison is located — for herself. That land thrived with “dusk, twilight — that’s what the island was in its long-buried heart.”

But after getting greedy for power, Theia and her court — as well as people with red hair who “looked alarmingly like Bryce’s father,” the Autumn King — migrated to Midgard, only to find themselves trapped under the reign of the very creatures they had fought to overthrow.

Silene was able to return to Prythian and escape the Asteri, but she concealed her power and the memory of ancestors vanished. The land of the former Dusk Court around her died, forming the barren isolation of the Prison. When Silene eventually married her mate, a High Lord of the Night Court, her firstborn son glowed with starlight inherited from her. “It was light of the evening star. The dusk star,” she says.
Bryce’s Starborn power is later described as a “dusk power,” a force the princes of Hel also call “starfire.”
How ‘Crescent City’ Connects to ‘Throne of Glass’

“House of Flame and Shadow” contains notable crossovers with “Throne of Glass,” Maas’ first series published in 2012. But many speculate that the world of “Crescent City” was first alluded to in “Kingdom of Ash,” the last book in the “Throne of Glass” series.

When Aelin falls between worlds — in the same instance she passes by Rhys and Feyre, as mentioned above — she also passes by a “world where a great city had been built along the curve of a river, the buildings impossibly tall and glimmering with lights.” It’s likely this is Lunathion, aka the titular Crescent City, which gets its name from the bend of the Istros River through it.
From there, though, most connections are seen in passing references and winks at the series.

The most overt connection between “Crescent City” and “Throne of Glass” comes in “House of Flame and Shadow” with the Under-King’s passing reference to Wyrd, which he describes as his home planet’s equivalent of Midgard’s Urd, the goddess of fate.

Wyrd, however, isn’t a goddess, but a “force that governed worlds. A cauldron of life, brimming with the language of creation,” says Under-King, the head of Lunathion’s Bone Quarter and leader of the House of Flame and Shadow.

In “Throne of Glass,” Wyrd, pronounced “word,” is indeed everywhere. The central conflict across the eight-book series centers on Aelin’s attempts to close the Wyrdgates, essentially portals between worlds (sound familiar?) by gathering all the Wyrdkeys. Her goal is to destroy the keys to prevent the Valg, demons that possess people and feed off their souls (again, sound familiar?), from coming to her world and conquering it with the power of Wyrdstone. She also learns to harness the power of Wyrdmarks, aka, magic runes.

It’s unclear if the Valg of “Throne of Glass” are the same as the Asteri/Dalgan, though both beings aim to conquer and consume. But “House of Flame and Shadow” does contain several references to the Asteri’s power over worlds as a “collar,” which is a major tool the Valg used to possess people, like Dorian.
After “House of Sky and Breath,” readers learned that shifters, including wolves like Ithan and Danika, are also Fae who just originated from a different world.

Once Ithan takes Hypaxia’s antidote to the Asteri’s power blocker in “House of Flame and Shadow,” he learns that his power wasn’t always just limited to shifting. He also has the power of wielding snow and ice.

The combination of an animal form and an elemental power is the prototype of the Fae found in “Throne of Glass,” suggesting shifters like Ithan came from the same world as Aelin. Fans of that series will remember Rowan Whitethorn could shift into a hawk and could wield wind.

Let’s also go back to the tale told by Silene, the daughter Queen Theia. When recounting to Bryce, Nesta and Azriel how Theia led a takeover of Midgard, she notes that the rifts opened once again and more Fae appeared “from another world this time.”

“They were Fae like us, but not,” Silene says. “The ears, the grace, the strength were identical, but they were shape-shifters, all of them. Each capable of turning into an animal. And each, even in their humanoid body, equipped with elongated canine teeth.”
Ithan, armed with his newly discovered powers, later takes on the Under-King directly.
